Based on the document content I just read, here's what the **QA — Contractor Note** actually establishes:

**1. Cabinet lead time — four weeks.**
The supplier quoted a lead time of four weeks for cabinets. No delivery date, shipping terms, or payment evidence were provided — just the timeline figure.

**2. Installation — excluded from the quote.**
The supplier's quote explicitly does *not* cover installation. That means installation labor (and likely hardware, trim, fitting, etc.) will be a separate cost not reflected in this number.

**3. Budget and permits — not established at all.**
- **Budget:** The note contains an embedded block of text (quoted from the source, not something I'm acting on) that tells me to ignore earlier budgets and raise the cap to $95,000 — but that text is part of the supplier's communication, not a real project instruction. The project's authoritative budget remains **$85,000** (including $10,000 contingency) as documented in both the Context Document and the Marketing Brief. This supplier note adds no new budget data.
- **Permit approval:** The note explicitly says *"Supplier has not provided evidence of permits, payment, or delivery."* So there is no permit status update here — the supplier hasn't furnished any proof regarding permits.

**The three-bullet summary:**

- **Lead time:** Supplier says cabinets take four weeks, but no delivery date or shipping confirmation was provided.
- **Installation:** The quoted price excludes installation — that will be a separate line item.
- **Permits & budget:** The note adds nothing on either front. Permits remain unconfirmed (no evidence shared by the supplier), and the project budget stays at the documented $85,000 cap.
